full_judgment: 41. In the face of the testimony of D.W.2 that the defendant No.1 had acquaintance with the plain- tiff No.1 and the averment in the written statement that the defendant No.1 had personal acquaintance with the plaintiff No.1 and gave him' personal loan of Tk. 45,000/-, the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that no evidence has been led by the defendants that the defendants were friendly or in any way connected with the defendants or they had any business transaction prior to 1973 nor the defendants disclosed anywhere in their pleadings and evidence any sort of clement that leads a person to believe that the plaintiff No. 1 took loan from the defendant No. 1 is perverse. The said averment in the written statement and the testimony of defendant No.2 lead to the conclusion that the defendant No.2 had friendly business relation with the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant No.1 gave personal loan of Tk. 45,000/- to plaintiff NO.1 which the latter paid by depositing the same in the personal account of defendant No. 1 and his son, but when the negotiation between the defendants and the plaintiffs for the sale of the suit property by the defendants to the plaintiffs failed in 1978 and the defendants refused to sell the suit property the plaintiffs filed the false suit for specific performance of contract taking advantage of the deposit of loan of Tk. 45,000/- by plaintiff No.1 in the personal account of defendant No. 1 and his son as per Ext. 1 and 1 (a). The plaintiffs have to prove their own case and discharge the burden of proof which is on them. The learned Advocate for the appellant has V not advanced any argument as to defect of parties and limitation and as such the findings of the learned Subordinate Judge thereon are upheld. They can not succeed on the weakness of the defence case. The learned Subordinate Judge has seriously erred in disposing of the suit on the erroneous view that be- cause of the weakness of the defence case the plaintiffs' case is proved. From the evidence on record it is apparent plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove their case of oral contract by reliable, convincing and independent evidence. In the above circumstances, it is found that the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge suffers fro in flaw and illegality calling for interference.
